title: The Papers: 'Pain beyond words' and 'Graduates face worst job market'
originalTitle: The Papers: 'Pain beyond words' and 'Graduates face worst job market'
content:
The front pages of the Times and the Daily Telegraph report that Prime Minister Andy Burnham will give Ukraine "secret blueprints" to produce long-range missiles. According to the Times, Scalp missiles are designed for attacks on high-value targets, external such as hardened bunkers and key infrastructure. The Telegraph says the move could convince other Western allies to follow suit, external. The Guardian warns though that it will "likely escalate tensions with Moscow, external at an already fraught time in UK-Russian relations".

The Sun features a picture of a smiling Princess of Wales, external on her way to church, with the paper saying the Royal Family put on a "united front" after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex announced they were returning to the UK. "We're all GRIN it together" is the headline. The i Paper describes the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge's comeback as a "royal reckoning", external - saying they will have to deal with the Palace "whether they like it or not".

The Daily Mail leads on a warning from the head of the National Crime Agency,, external Graeme Biggar, that it is "not safe" for children to go online. The paper says "terrifying" figures reveal up to 900 cases of suspected child sexual exploitation are flagged every day.

"No more", is the message from families of victims of drowning, external on the front of the Daily Mirror. In an open letter to the prime minister, they say "anyone can drown, but no one should". They are calling for Burnham to appoint a minister with responsibility for drowning prevention.

"Thor blimey" is a caption in the Daily Mail as it features pictures of the Manchester City and Norway footballer Erling Haaland, external having his trademark long hair cut. The Daily Express considers whether Haaland's new "close-cropped look" may have left him with "food for thought, external" after failing to score in yesterday's 2-1 victory over Bournemouth. The Daily Star's editorial has no such concerns - saying he remains a "cut above"., external
